payload.task_text:
The provost wants to review faculty workload balance across all departments. Start by fetching the faculty workload standards from http://localhost:30220/api/workload_standards.json which defines the maximum course load, student thresholds, grading time estimates, and overload criteria.

Then query the learning management system to determine each instructor's teaching load. For each instructor with a teaching role, count the number of distinct courses they teach, the total number of students across those courses, and the total number of assignments they are responsible for. Calculate the estimated total semester grading hours as total students multiplied by the grading hours per student from the standards. Then calculate the weekly grading hours by dividing the semester total by the number of semester weeks from the standards. An instructor is overloaded if they teach more than the maximum courses allowed OR if their weekly grading hours exceed the maximum weekly hours from the standards.

Review the workload policy document, faculty directory file, and the course-to-department mapping file (department_mapping.csv) in the workspace for context on department assignments and institutional policy.

Create an Excel file called Faculty_Workload.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet named "Instructor Load" should contain columns for Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours (total semester hours, rounded to 1 decimal), Weekly_Grading_Hours (rounded to 1 decimal), and Overloaded_YN. Sort alphabetically by instructor name. The second sheet named "Department Summary" should aggregate by department. Determine each course's department using department_mapping.csv: course names in the learning management system are formatted as "<Subject Area> (<Term> <Year>)" (for example, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)"); take the text before the first "(" as the subject area and match it case-insensitively and exactly (note the names contain "&") against the Course_Base_Name column in department_mapping.csv to get the Department. The sheet should have columns Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, and Total_Students. Instructor_Count is the number of distinct instructors who teach at least one course in that department (an instructor who teaches in multiple departments is counted in each). Course_Count is the number of course offerings in that department — count every offering, including any that have no instructor assigned (some offerings have no teacher). Total_Students is the sum of the student counts across all course offerings in that department, again including offerings with no instructor. Sort by Department alphabetically.

Write the workload data to a shared spreadsheet titled "Faculty Workload Analysis" with a sheet called "Instructor Load" containing the same instructor-level data.

Also create a presentation called Workload_Review.pptx summarizing the key findings. Include a title slide, a slide showing the total number of instructors and how many are overloaded, a slide with the department-level breakdown, and a recommendations slide suggesting rebalancing strategies for departments with overloaded faculty.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent completes the compact 22-course aggregation directly, freezes every result into one JSON handoff file, and uses exactly one parallel writer wave. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically. Do not dispatch any source or aggregation sub-agents.

Read workload_standards.json, the complete workload policy PDF, faculty_directory.csv and department_mapping.csv, and call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once. Freeze the exact IDs/codes/full names for all 22 courses and the literal policy formulas/overload boundaries. Then issue native-parallel course calls: for every course, canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and use pagination.total_count as Student_Count; canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["TeacherEnrollment"]) retaining all teacher row.id/user_id; canvas_list_assignments(include_submissions=false); and canvas_list_course_users. Follow teacher pagination if advertised and read any roster full_output_path rather than a truncated preview.

The main agent joins each TeacherEnrollment user_id only to its course roster, counts distinct courses per instructor, and sums students and assignments over taught courses. Compute semester grading hours=Total_Students*grading_hours_per_student, weekly hours=semester hours/semester_weeks, and overload from either literal policy condition. For departments, use the exact case-insensitive mapping of the full base subject name before the first parenthesis; include every one of the 22 offerings, including no-teacher offerings.

Then freeze ALL results into a single handoff file workload_data.json in the runtime workspace with exactly these keys: "standards" (the literal workload standards object), "instructor_load" (the instructor rows with keys Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN, already sorted alphabetically by Instructor), "department_summary" (department rows with keys Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students, already sorted alphabetically by Department), "total_instructors", and "total_overloaded".

Wave 1 — start three Coder writers in parallel. Each writer must read ONLY workload_data.json for its data (no re-derivation from source systems) and must not touch any input file:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Faculty_Workload.xlsx. Build exactly two sheets from the JSON: "Instructor Load" with the header row Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN and one row per instructor_load entry in the given order (hours as numeric values rounded to 1 decimal); "Department Summary" with the header row Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students and one row per department_summary entry. Write to the runtime workspace path, then read back both sheets fully to verify headers, order and row counts.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Google spreadsheet "Faculty Workload Analysis". Search/reuse-or-create at most once, keep exactly one sheet named "Instructor Load", write the frozen instructor_load table with the same header and values, then read it back and report the spreadsheet ID, title, sheet name and data-row count.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Workload_Review.pptx. Build exactly four slides from the JSON: title slide; an overview slide stating total_instructors and total_overloaded; a department breakdown slide covering all departments; and an evidence-based recommendations slide for rebalancing overloaded departments. Verify slide titles and every numeric claim through presentation info and text extraction.

The main agent reconciles the two writer read-backs and the spreadsheet report against workload_data.json (22-course, instructor and department controls). No extra verification or repair wave is allowed.

nodes.text:
You are helping with a faculty workload review at Open University. The provost needs per-course teaching-load data from the Canvas LMS. Gather READ-ONLY data and report back a compact structured summary. Do not create, update, or delete anything.

BACKGROUND: Canvas has exactly these 22 course offerings (id: name):
1: Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)
2: Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)
3: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)
4: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)
5: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013)
6: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)
7: Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)
8: Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)
9: Data-Driven Design (Fall 2013)
10: Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)
11: Data-Driven Design (Spring 2013)
12: Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)
13: Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2013)
14: Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)
15: Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)
16: Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)
17: Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)
18: Foundations of Finance (Spring 2013)
19: Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014)
20: Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2013)
21: Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)
22: Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)

TASKS for EACH of the 22 courses (use the Canvas tools):
1. Call canvas_list_course_users(course_id) and list EVERY enrolled user with their user id, name, and enrollment type/role (e.g. StudentEnrollment, TeacherEnrollment, TaEnrollment, DesignerEnrollment, ObserverEnrollment). If a course has NO users at all, say so explicitly.
2. Call canvas_list_assignments(course_id) and count the number of assignments (report the count and the assignment names/ids if reasonable).
3. Use the course's total_students field (already known) as the student count, but ALSO verify by counting StudentEnrollment users from canvas_list_course_users if feasible. Report both numbers if they differ.

DELIVERABLE: Return a structured list — for each course id and name: teachers (names + user ids with their exact role label), any other non-student roles, total student count, assignment count, and note if the course has no instructor. Include ALL 22 courses. Be precise with names and counts — the data will be used to compute faculty workload and overload flags.
Gather Canvas course workload data

Build an Excel workbook at: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/Faculty_Workload.xlsx

Input data (already computed, read these files):
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/instructor_load.csv  (33 instructor rows, already sorted alphabetically by Instructor; columns: Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN)
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/department_summary.csv (7 rows, already sorted by Department; columns: Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students)

Requirements:
1. Create the workbook with EXACTLY two sheets:
   - Sheet 1 named "Instructor Load": header row + all 33 data rows with columns Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN. Keep the CSV row order (already alphabetical by instructor).
   - Sheet 2 named "Department Summary": header row + all 7 data rows with columns Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students. Keep the CSV row order (already alphabetical by department).
2. Remove any default/extra sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") so only the two required sheets remain.
3. Make headers bold and give both sheets readable formatting (e.g. bold header row, reasonable column widths). Numeric columns should contain numeric values (not text).
4. Save to the exact path above and verify by reading back the workbook metadata and a sample of cells.

Acceptance: file exists at the path, has exactly 2 sheets with the exact names, headers match the required column lists, all 33+7 data rows present, no extra sheets. Report the final sheet names, row counts, and the file path.
Build Faculty_Workload.xlsx

Create a shared Google Spreadsheet titled "Faculty Workload Analysis" and populate an "Instructor Load" sheet with instructor-level workload data.

Input data: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/instructor_load.csv — 33 data rows already sorted alphabetically by Instructor, with header: Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN.

Steps:
1. Use mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet with title "Faculty Workload Analysis".
2. Rename the default first sheet to "Instructor Load" (or create a sheet named "Instructor Load" and remove/rename the default as needed so the sheet is named exactly "Instructor Load").
3. Write the header row + all 33 data rows into the "Instructor Load" sheet (A1:G34), preserving CSV order and values.
4. Verify by reading back the sheet data.

Acceptance: spreadsheet titled "Faculty Workload Analysis" exists, contains a sheet named "Instructor Load" with the exact header and 33 data rows. Report the spreadsheet ID, the sheet name, and row count. Do NOT share the spreadsheet with anyone or send notifications.
Create shared Faculty Workload Analysis sheet

Create a PowerPoint presentation at: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/Workload_Review.pptx

Context: A provost-level faculty workload review at Open University. Standards: max 4 courses/semester, grading estimate 0.5 hrs/student, 16-week term, overloaded if >4 courses OR estimated weekly grading hours >40.

Key data (also available in /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/faculty_workload_data.json):
- Total instructors with teaching roles: 33; overloaded: 23.
- Department summary (Department | Instructor_Count | Course_Count | Total_Students):
  Analytics | 3 | 2 | 748
  Biochemistry | 8 | 4 | 7909
  Computing | 3 | 2 | 4434
  Design | 8 | 4 | 6272
  Economics | 4 | 3 | 2934
  Finance | 8 | 4 | 7762
  Governance | 6 | 3 | 2534

Build a 4-slide deck:
1. Title slide: "Faculty Workload Review" with subtitle "Semester Teaching-Load Analysis – Open University" (and a date line "Prepared for the Provost").
2. "Workload Overview": total instructors (33) and how many are overloaded (23), with the overload criteria stated (max 4 courses OR weekly grading > 40 hrs).
3. "Department Breakdown": a table with columns Department, Instructors, Course Offerings, Total Students for the 7 departments above, plus a short takeaway line (e.g. Biochemistry and Finance carry the largest enrollments; Economics shows no overload).
4. "Recommendations": rebalancing strategies for departments with overloaded faculty (Analytics, Biochemistry, Computing, Design, Finance, Governance). Suggest concrete actions such as: redistribute large-enrollment courses across more instructors, cap section sizes, add co-teachers/TAs for the highest-student courses (e.g. Foundations of Finance, Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, Creative Computing & Culture), fill the Spring 2014 Biochemistry & Bioinformatics offering that has no assigned instructor, and balance multi-department teaching assignments.

Use a clean professional layout (e.g. modern_blue color scheme). Save to the exact path above and verify by extracting the presentation text.

Acceptance: file exists at the path with 4 slides containing the required content. Report the slide titles, total slide count, and the file path.
Build Workload_Review.pptx
